row.claim: The chain was stopped cleanly and completely. Job 305318 ended COMPLETED with ExitCode 0:0 after 18:39:50, having exited the loop through the STOP brake at a cycle boundary (synchronous_loop_9x9.sh:426-429) rather than through a signal, so finalize() ran in full: the stage monitor was stopped and drained (64137 ps samples, 13342 gpu samples) and .failcount was reset to 0. The queued afterany successor 314831 was cancelled first, at 12:59:09, before the brake was set at 12:59:50, and shows CANCELLED with Elapsed 00:00:00; this was necessary because on the wrapper version that ran, the rc=0 clean-exit branch of finalize() (loop.sbatch:560-563) does not cancel the successor. No ktg-loop job remains in the queue and none was resubmitted. Terminal state: .cycles_completed 249 (157 cycles in link 1, 92 in link 2), .chain_depth 2, .failcount 0, .breaker_tripped absent, STOP present, 93 accepted exports, 3 rejected, modelstobetested and torchmodels_toexport both empty. The run trained 28950784 samples (last metric row 28942080) and last exported at 28711040 samples, so the trainer checkpoint is 239744 samples ahead of the newest net -- the normal resume position. Cumulative self-play is 322600 games (157 x 1000 in link 1, 92 x 1800 in link 2, read from the wrapper logs' per-cycle progress counter, whose per-cycle maxima are exactly {1000} and {1800}); 183443 of those games survive the retention window and are saved. The latest accepted net, t9-s28711040-d3032547 (model.bin.gz sha256 4cbedf24ac86f97f1d15ec69706161e7ac98c3f3a2fddadb543d40bea897f49c), is also the best of all 93 exports on both learned metrics -- p0loss 1.468345 and pacc1 0.546604, computed by joining every export's sample count to train/t9/metrics_train.json, which matched exactly for 93 of 93 exports. Ranked by raw vloss alone the minimum is t9-s1762560-d595534 at 0.569050, an early net whose p0loss is 2.734 and pacc1 0.362; raw vloss is therefore not a strength ordering, which is the reading the c14 match (r_c14_latest_beats_best_by_loss_9x9) established independently. All of it is saved at /home/schmidt/ssci-haiyangw/ktg-checkpoints/2026-09-06_stop: 7683842860 B in 10957 files, of which 10956 are listed in MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 ef75ba6c3155593a687daaf70e0b3ef5f0c705af6ec17974e8f12bc0a7efc4d2) and all 10956 verify. Every copied component was compared source-to-destination on both byte count and file count before the manifest was written and all ten matched exactly.

execution.note: run by the WORKER by hand; the validator must re-run it before admitting. It is idempotent and touches nothing -- it only reads sacct, squeue, the wrapper log, runs/p1 and the checkpoint.

each export's sample count identifies its metric row exactly; 93 of 93 exports matched a row at the same nsamp, so no interpolation or nearest-neighbour fallback was used in ranking the nets

budget.env:55 still reads KTG_KEEP_SELFPLAY_GENERATIONS=3 while the shuffle window sits at 442100 rows, inside the KEEP=60 band, with 38 selfplay net directories surviving; whatever holds those directories is not that knob, and the retention-60 result stands conditional rather than checked

the vloss-stability half of the retention test is not met -- max |vloss step| inside the >=380000-row window is 0.006765 against a stated 0.005 -- and there is still no validation split, so TD-loss trigger (iii) was never evaluable at any read of this run
the checkpoint is a single copy on one filesystem. It is hash-manifested but not replicated; a second copy elsewhere would be needed before the scratch tree is cleared
row.notes: The stop was ordered, not triggered by any condition in the run. Nothing in the chain's own state called for stopping: the circuit breaker was not tripped, the storage guard had passed 251 of 251 invocations, and read 14 forty minutes earlier had recorded that the 19-export policy stall had just ended with new records on both metrics. The successor was cancelled before the brake was set specifically because the wrapper version that was running does not cancel it on a clean exit; getting that order wrong would have started a fresh 23.5 h allocation that then immediately exited on the brake. Time from the brake to the loop's exit was 3 min 16 s, well inside the 25-minute fallback, so the fallback (scancel of the running job) was never used and the last cycle finished its train and export stages normally.
